review_title: AI might be good for some, but for me it was the end.
review_text:

I had no need for ai when it launched. It was unobtrusive, however, so I carried on. Then, a badly implemented update caused a piece of writing I had worked on for hours to, with an easy keyboard stumble, be completely rewritten. Completely. Hours of work chewed up and spit out into slush. :/ I promptly closed the app and stopped writing in it.  

Years later, I have found a software I like better, with no intrusive ai and no cloud services, so my notes are no longer at risk in a server I don't have access to. I have zero faith that notion has kept anything I ever wrote secure. They continue to say one thing and do another. I am done. 

In logging in to transfer my notes, I notice that the program is buggy and slow in ways it never was years ago. Buffers like crazy. It's actually kind of heartbreaking to see how far this app has fallen.

There are better options out there, with more security and better customization. Even if you want ai in a notes app, there are more clean and helpful options that do not compromise your experience. Why pick notion? I never will again.

I’ve been a Notion power user since about 2018. I rely on it for hours every day. The overall trajectory of the platform has been great since then, but the mobile app has always had issues. And it seems they are getting worse. Just about every app update these days introduces major workflow breaking bugs. For example, it worked perfectly yesterday until I updated to the latest version today, and now mobile dictation is completely broken. 

Currently, with many multi select properties, sometimes opening the selection window completely crashes the app and it must be manually restarted.

Each update is like Russian Roulette: perhaps you’ll gain some small feature, and hopefully you won’t also get a new bug that completely interferes with usability. A bit hyperbolic? Sure. My business runs on this platform and bugs that break basic usability cost me. 

Will update this review if they manage to roll out 3 consecutive updates without breaking anything major.

review_text:
اعطيت التطبيق نجمة واحدة لكوني لم استطع استخدامه او تجربته! بسبب مشكلة اتجاه النص العربي (RTL) و بسبب عدم توفّر واجهة عربية (Arabic UI)، و في ادناه تحليل المشكلة و الحل الذي ينبغي على المطورين اعتماده.

- وصف المشكلة (Issue Description):
    
    يعاني المستخدمون العرب من قلب اتجاه السطر وتخبّط المحاذاة أثناء الكتابة بالعربية داخل نَوشَن (Notion). يظهر الخلل خصوصًا عند إدراج كلمات إنجليزية قصيرة داخل سطر عربي، مما يؤدي إلى اضطراب اتجاه النص وعدم اتساق العرض.
    
- خطوات إعادة الإنتاج (Steps to Reproduce):
    1. اكتب سطرًا عربيًا يبدأ بحرف عربي.
    2. أضف مصطلحًا إنجليزيًا بين قوسين بعد كلمة عربية مثل: اسمي احمد (ahmed) وأسكن بغداد (Baghdad).
    3. لاحظ تغيّر اتجاه السطر أو اختلاط المحاذاة يمينًا ويسارًا، خاصة عند نسخ السطر أو تعديله.
- النتيجة الحالية (Actual Result):
    
    اختلال اتجاه السطر وتخبّط المحاذاة، مما يصعّب القراءة والكتابة ويشوّه التنسيق.
    
- النتيجة المتوقعة (Expected Result):
    
    ثبات اتجاه النص العربي من اليمين إلى اليسار (RTL) حتى مع وجود مصطلحات إنجليزية قصيرة ضمن السطر، مع محاذاة مستقرة وموثوقة.
    
- الأثر (Impact):
    
    تجربة الكتابة للمستخدم العربي تتأثر سلبًا، ويصعب استخدام نَوشَن (Notion) لإدارة المحتوى اليومي أو الاحترافي. هذا يسبب إحباطًا ويجبر البعض على التوقف عن استخدام التطبيق.
    
- البيئة (Environment):
    
    لغة الكتابة العربية (Arabic). المشكلة تظهر في الويب (Web) وتطبيق الهاتف (Mobile App) على حد سواء بحسب ملاحظات المستخدمين.
    
- أمثلة سطرية (Examples):
    - اسمي احمد (ahmed) وأسكن بغداد (Baghdad)
    - سكربت الحلقة (Script) والعناصر الأساسية (Key Points)
- طلب التحسين (Request):
    1. دعم كامل لاتجاه النص العربي من اليمين إلى اليسار (RTL) داخل المحرّر.
    2. إضافة خيار لغة عربية للواجهة (Arabic UI) ضمن الإعدادات (Settings).
    3. تحسين التعامل مع المصطلحات الإنجليزية القصيرة داخل السطور العربية دون إفساد الاتجاه.
- ملاحظات إضافية (Additional Notes):
    
    يفضّل توفير إعداد لإجبار اتجاه الفقرة عربيًا عند الحاجة، وخيار تنسيق سريع يضمن عدم قلب الاتجاه حتى مع الرموز والروابط.

review_title: Great... If You Enjoy Being Locked Out of Your Own Business
review_text:
To be honest, Trello used to be a great productivity tool — until Atlassian showed up with their magic trick: locking paying users out of their accounts with surprise 2FA prompts nobody ever set up. Brilliant.

Imagine running a business, managing projects, staying on top of deliverables… and then suddenly you can’t log in on desktop because Trello decided you should have 2FA credentials that you never received. No recovery codes. No setup flow. No warning. Just *poof* — productivity gone.

The cherry on top? You can’t even contact support because you need to log in to do that — which you obviously can’t, because, well, 2FA. I'm two days behind on major work, stuck on a mobile app UI that feels like it was designed as an afterthought, and completely locked out of critical project boards on desktop.

This isn’t a bug — this is a UX disaster dressed as a “security feature.” And while Trello’s parent company Atlassian might think they’re tightening security, they’re really just tightening the noose around their own product’s credibility.

For a platform built on the promise of helping businesses stay organized, this rollout was anything but. If you’re running a serious business, look elsewhere — until Trello figures out how to secure accounts *without* locking out their users in the process.
